accuracy.evidence: All equations atom-checked: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O (C 1/1, H 4/4, O 4/4), 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O (O 6/6), 2CH₄ + 2O₂ → 2C + 4H₂O (O 4/4), C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Alkane items use CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with n CO₂ and n + 1 H₂O per molecule, checked at the range corners (p2/p3 n = 1..8, m4 2n for n = 1..6, m7 2n + 2 for n = 2..7). Chemistry matches AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462 4.7.1.3 (complete combustion of hydrocarbons) and 4.9.3.1 (carbon monoxide and soot from incomplete combustion), and the topic's three evidence lines. CO facts from the NHS and HSE: colourless, odourless, binds haemoglobin about 200–250 times more strongly than oxygen (the lab says 'about 200'), the mains-gas smell is an added odorant. The yellow luminous Bunsen flame is glowing soot and cooler than the blue flame; incomplete combustion releases less energy. Tests: condensation on a cold surface for water, limewater turning milky for CO₂ (CO does not).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented GCSE errors: less oxygen gives more CO₂ (step 3 prediction, tag 'oxygen'), hydrogen gas as a product (step 3 'Hydrogen gas', tag 'hydrogen', p1), yellow flame is hotter (step 1 'It turns blue and hotter', tag 'hot', p4, m8), CO can be smelled or seen (step 4 prediction, tag 'smell', m6), CO harms like an acid or only as soot (tag 'co', p5, m9), mixing CO with CO₂ in the limewater test (m5), and balancing O₂ without counting every H₂O's oxygen (step 2 prediction with 1 and 4 as tempting options, tag 'balance', m1).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagburn is about oxygen supply deciding the products: a Bunsen collar slider that changes flame colour, soot particles and the product list; an atom-tally balancer for methane; a 2/3/4 O₂ slider for two CH₄ that redraws CO₂ → CO → C molecules; red blood cells whose oxygen seats CO takes until an alarm sounds; and two product tests. flagalktr (boiling point and flammability trends), flagalk (alkane structure), flagalcox and reactlab (reaction types) do none of this; the 6-shingle gate passes under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner changes the oxygen and sees the result before the text names it: flame colour, soot and product list change with the collar; the ✓/✗ tally shows which atom is unbalanced as molecules are added; the molecules on the product side change from CO₂ to CO to C as O₂ is cut while water stays; the 'cells carrying O₂' count falls as CO arrives and the alarm only sounds once all seats are taken; droplets and milky limewater appear only when each test is run. Each step closes with the rule just shown.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: closing the air hole makes the flame 'blue and hotter' (it goes yellow and sooty), one CH₄ needs '1' or '4' O₂ (the tally only balances at 2), less oxygen gives 'more carbon dioxide' or 'hydrogen gas' (CO and C appear, water stays), and 'CO smells strongly, so people leave' (the room fills with no warning until the alarm).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six feedback messages keyed to the slip: 'oxygen' (CO forms when oxygen is short), 'hydrogen' (hydrogen joins oxygen to make water), 'hot' (yellow is glowing soot and cooler), 'balance' (count O in every H₂O and CO₂), 'smell' (CO is odourless; the gas smell is an added odorant) and 'co' (binds haemoglobin). In-lab feedback names the unbalanced element with both counts and explains each oxygen setting.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the readability limits (kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5). Kid text uses short sentences and introduces each formula next to its name (carbon dioxide, CO₂); 'haemoglobin' is kept for the adult text and the lab says 'oxygen seats on red blood cells'. Canvas text is 13–22 px; buttons are short (Open the air hole, + O₂, 3 O₂, Let CO in).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12%). Kid paragraphs: what a hydrocarbon fuel is, complete combustion with the methane equation, incomplete combustion with CO and soot, why CO is dangerous. Adult paragraphs: AQA spec placement, four balanced equations and the tests, six named mistakes with the haemoglobin figure, and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark themes for every step after Show me. Fixed after the first shots: the flame title and product list were clipped at the right edge (title moved to the top centre, list at 13 px), the air-hole labels overlapped the burner base (moved under the slider), the cell count overlapped the CO count (moved), CO and O₂ on red cells were hard to see (pale backing added), the alarm used a theme red with white text in dark mode (now fixed #b91c1c), and the two test results overlapped (now on two lines).

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Open/Close the air hole, + / − O₂ and H₂O, 4/3/2 O₂, Let CO in, the two tests. The canvas aria-label and visible description update with each change through tell(). The walk gate's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA, both themes, desktop and iPhone 13) reported no violations and no console or page errors.
